prompt: Two straight bike paths cross. Which statement about the pair of vertical angles formed at the crossing is ALWAYS true, no matter how the paths are angled?

choices.label: They are adjacent — they share a side

hint: Vertical angles sit across the crossing from each other, not next to each other.

hints.text: Vertical angles sit across the crossing from each other, not next to each other.
It is the angles NEXT to each other — linear pairs — that add to $180^\circ$.

explanation: Vertical angles are the pairs directly opposite each other where two lines cross.
Each of them forms a linear pair with the same neighbor angle, so each equals $180^\circ$ minus that neighbor — which forces them to be equal.
They are therefore always congruent. (They only add to $180^\circ$ in the special case where both are $90^\circ$.)

alternativeExplanations.title: Test an extreme case
steps: Imagine the paths crossing at a very sharp angle, making a $20^\circ$ vertical pair.
Those two add to $40^\circ$, not $180^\circ$ or $90^\circ$ — but they are equal to each other, which is the part that never changes.
